headline: Remote access gateways under attack as Docker Hub and GitLab ship critical fixes
standfirst: Two internet-facing remote access products are under active attack, Docker Hub and GitLab disclosed critical flaws, and the breach file runs from warm supermarket fridges to tampered crypto wallets.
bodyMarkdown:
## Actively exploited

Two warnings about edge infrastructure. Ivanti told customers to immediately patch an actively exploited zero-day in Connect Secure, its remote access gateway [[s10]]. The supplied material gives no CVE, CVSS score or affected versions, so the scope of exposure cannot be judged from it. SonicWall's SMA 1000 appliances are being targeted through a maximum-severity server-side request forgery flaw [[s32]], again with no identifier supplied here. Analysis: both cases fit the pattern that matters most to defenders — a flaw in an appliance that sits on the internet by design, where patching is the only lever the sources imply. Neither is attributed to a named actor; treat the missing technical identifiers as something to confirm against the vendors' own advisories, not as an absence of risk.

## Vulnerabilities

Docker Hub carried a critical incorrect-privilege-assignment flaw, CVE-2026-105445, rated 9.4 under CVSS 4.0 [[s11]]. Per the structured record, an authenticated attacker could reassign a personal access token they controlled to another Docker Hub user without rotating or revoking the token secret; the unchanged token then authenticated to the registry as the recipient and could pull, push or delete images within its scopes, including organization repositories. There is no indication in the supplied intelligence that it was exploited.

GitLab patched a CVSS 10.0 issue that, under certain conditions, could have allowed an unauthenticated user to execute arbitrary code on the server via a specially crafted regular expression in CI/CD, affecting Community and Enterprise Editions [[s29]]. No CVE ID was supplied. Self-hosted instances are the relevant exposure.

## Breaches

Attackers took remote control of fridges and freezers at hundreds of French supermarkets and warmed them, forcing stores to discard food [[s27]]. Access came through the Danfoss controller that runs a store's refrigeration and that maintenance firms manage remotely — a physical-world outcome reached through a remote management path. Meta said hackers took code and personal data belonging to 1,500 people, mostly US employees, who are being offered credit monitoring [[s9]]. Ledger said wallets sold through a Southeast Asian reseller had an implant that let outsiders drain funds, with recovery-phrase theft reported as the mechanism [[s16]] — a company statement, with no technical detail supplied.

## Research

North Korean hackers have been targeting Ukrainian experts in diplomacy, security and international policy, reportedly for intelligence on Russia's war, amid Pyongyang's growing military cooperation with Moscow [[s12]]. The excerpt offers no tooling, victim counts or named intrusion set, so the operational picture stays thin; the attribution is the source's.

selected.title: Docker Hub flaw let attackers impersonate users, tamper with images
selected.excerpt: Docker has disclosed a critical vulnerability (CVE-2026-105445) in Docker Hub that let attackers access another user's container repositories using a personal access token (PAT). [...]

nvd.description: An Incorrect Privilege Assignment vulnerability in Docker Hub's account-to-organization conversion feature allowed an authenticated attacker to reassign a personal access token (PAT) they controlled to another Docker Hub user without rotating or revoking the token secret. The unchanged PAT then authenticated to the registry as the recipient and could pull, push, or delete images, within its scopes, in repositories accessible to that user, including organization repositories.

selected.angle: Critical Docker Hub flaw allowed attackers to reassign personal access tokens and tamper with container images, posing a supply chain threat.

selected.title: Attackers Heat French Supermarket Fridges Up to 50°C by Hijacking Danfoss Controllers
selected.excerpt: Attackers took remote control of fridges and freezers at hundreds of French supermarkets on the night of October 11 and warmed them, forcing stores to throw food away, several retail chains said. The attackers reached them through the controller that runs all of a store's fridges and freezers, a device made by Danish company Danfoss that maintenance firms can manage remotely. Les Mousquetaires
selected.angle: Attackers hijacked refrigeration controllers across hundreds of European supermarkets, causing physical disruption and food spoilage.
